kjv: Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed
mine: For 2,300 evenings and mornings. Then the sanctuary shall be restored to its rightful state
note: erev boqer "evening morning" likely counts the twice-daily tamid offerings (1,150 days, about the Maccabean desecration); KJV's "days" doubled the span and underlies historicist date-setting; nitsdaq means "be set right/vindicated", while "cleansed" comes from the LXX.

mine: Without warning he shall destroy many
note: beshalvah "in (their) security/unawares" describes surprise attacks on those at ease, not destruction by means of peace.
